## Week 9 — Foundation of Intensity

Week 9 introduces the new techniques at moderate loads. The client needs one week to learn the new training formats before loads are pushed to their maximum.

---

### Session 1 — Full Body Strength with Contrast Training (Monday)

**Warm-up (10 minutes):**
5 minutes assault bike or rowing machine at moderate pace, building to 70% max HR by the end. Then: band pull-aparts 2 × 15, hip circles 10 each direction, bodyweight Romanian deadlift 2 × 10, goblet squat 2 × 10, inchworm walk-outs 5 reps.

The warm-up in Phase 3 is longer and more thorough than in previous phases because the training intensity demands it. A client going into contrast training or cluster sets with an inadequate warm-up is at significantly elevated injury risk.

**Main Work — Contrast Pairs:**

*Contrast Pair 1 — Lower Body Strength and Power*
- **A1: Barbell Back Squat** — 4 sets × 5 reps. Heavy load — approximately 75–80% of estimated 1 rep max. Rest 15 seconds after the squat set.
- **A2: Jump Squat (bodyweight or light goblet)** — 4 sets × 6 reps. Immediately after the squat. Full depth, maximum explosive effort on the way up, soft landing. Rest 2 minutes 30 seconds before the next contrast pair.

The jump squat after a heavy barbell squat will feel dramatically more powerful than a jump squat performed cold. This is post-activation potentiation in action. Coach the client to focus on maximum explosiveness on every jump rep.

*Contrast Pair 2 — Upper Body Push Strength and Power*
- **B1: Dumbbell Bench Press** — 4 sets × 6 reps. Heavy load, 3-second eccentric. Rest 15 seconds.
- **B2: Plyometric Push-Up** — 4 sets × 5 reps. Hands leave the floor on each rep. If full plyometric push-ups are not yet achievable, use an incline plyometric push-up with hands on a bench. Rest 2 minutes before the next pair.

*Contrast Pair 3 — Hip Hinge Strength and Power*
- **C1: Trap Bar Deadlift** — 4 sets × 4 reps. Heaviest deadlift loads of the programme so far. Rest 15 seconds.
- **C2: Kettlebell Swing** — 4 sets × 8 reps. 16–20 kg kettlebell. Explosive hip drive, not a squat. Rest 2 minutes 30 seconds.

*Contrast Pair 4 — Upper Body Pull*
- **D1: Weighted Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up** — 4 sets × 6 reps. Heavy load. Rest 15 seconds.
- **D2: Explosive Inverted Row** — 4 sets × 6 reps. Using a Smith machine bar or TRX set at hip height. Pull explosively so the chest leaves the bar momentarily at the top. Rest 90 seconds.

**Metabolic Finisher — Loaded Carry Complex (10 minutes):**

Set up two sets of heavy dumbbells or a loaded trap bar. Complete the following sequence with 60 seconds rest between rounds. Aim for 3–4 complete rounds within the 10-minute window.

- Farmer's Carry — 30 metres (heavy dumbbells, one in each hand)
- Suitcase Carry — 20 metres each side (one heavy dumbbell, core braced against lateral flexion)
- Rack Carry — 20 metres (dumbbells held at shoulder height, elbows up)

The loaded carry finisher elevates heart rate significantly, drives additional metabolic stress, and has a pronounced post-exercise glucose-lowering effect that extends well into the recovery period.

**Cool-down:** 8 minutes. Static stretching — hip flexors, hamstrings, thoracic spine, lats, chest. Do not skip the cool-down in Phase 3. The intensity of these sessions means the parasympathetic recovery response is important for blood glucose stabilisation after training.

**Post-session blood glucose check:** Mandatory in Week 9 as the client adapts to the new intensity level. High-intensity training can cause an acute glucose rise during the session that then drops significantly in the 30–60 minutes post-session. She needs to be aware of this pattern.

---

### Session 2 — High-Intensity Conditioning — Density Block Format (Tuesday)

This session replaces the strength-endurance circuit of the original Phase 3 with a more demanding density block format.

**Warm-up (8 minutes):**
3 minutes rowing machine building to 75% max HR. Then: leg swings, hip circles, arm circles, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 push-ups, 5 inchworms.

**Block 1 — Lower Body Density Block (10 minutes)**

Set a timer for 10 minutes. Complete as many rounds as possible of the following three exercises, resting only as needed to maintain form. Record total rounds completed.

- Goblet Squat — 12 reps (moderate-heavy weight)
- Romanian Deadlift (dumbbells) — 10 reps
- Reverse Lunge — 8 reps each leg

Rest 3 minutes between blocks.

**Block 2 — Upper Body Density Block (10 minutes)**

- Dumbbell Row — 10 reps each arm
- Push-Up (weighted if possible — plate on back) — 12 reps
- Face Pull (cable) — 15 reps

Rest 3 minutes between blocks.

**Block 3 — Full Body Density Block (10 minutes)**

- Kettlebell Swing — 15 reps
- Box Step-Up (weighted) — 10 reps each leg
- Battle Ropes — 20 seconds maximum effort
- Plank with Alternating Shoulder Tap — 10 taps each side

**Cool-down:** 8 minutes stretching and foam rolling.

**Tracking:** Record total rounds for each block every week. The goal is to beat the previous week's score. This creates objective progressive overload without increasing load or volume — the client is simply doing more work in the same time period.

---

### Session 3 — Full Body Strength with Cluster Sets (Wednesday)

**Warm-up (10 minutes):** As per Session 1.

**Main Work — Cluster Sets on Primary Lifts, Supersets on Accessories:**

*Primary Movement 1 — Cluster Set Deadlift*
- **Trap Bar or Conventional Deadlift** — 4 cluster sets. Each cluster set = 2 reps, 15-second rest, 2 reps, 15-second rest, 1 rep. That is 5 total reps per cluster set with intra-set rest. Load should be approximately 80–85% of estimated 1 rep max — heavier than she could lift for 5 continuous reps. Rest 3 minutes between cluster sets.

This is the most technically demanding element of the session. Coach each rep individually. The intra-set rest allows partial phosphocreatine resynthesis, enabling heavier loads and better technique on every rep.

*Primary Movement 2 — Cluster Set Hip Thrust*
- **Barbell Hip Thrust** — 4 cluster sets. Each cluster = 3 reps, 10-second rest, 3 reps. 6 total reps per cluster. Load at approximately 80% estimated max. Rest 2 minutes 30 seconds between cluster sets.

*Superset 1 — Posterior Chain Accessories*
- **A1: Nordic Hamstring Curl (or lying leg curl with slow eccentric)** — 3 sets × 8 reps. 4-second eccentric. Rest 10 seconds.
- **A2: Glute Kickback (cable)** — 3 sets × 12 reps each leg. Rest 90 seconds.

*Superset 2 — Upper Body Pull*
- **B1: Seated Cable Row** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Heavy, full retraction. Rest 10 seconds.
- **B2: Rear Delt Fly (dumbbell)** — 4 sets × 15 reps. Light weight, controlled. Rest 75 seconds.

*Superset 3 — Core Anti-Rotation*
- **C1: Pallof Press** — 3 sets × 12 reps each side. Rest 10 seconds.
- **C2: Dead Bug with Dumbbell** — 3 sets × 8 reps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Metabolic Finisher — Loaded Carry Complex (10 minutes):** As per Session 1 but increase carry distances by 5 metres each.

---

### Session 4 — High-Intensity Conditioning — Interval Escalation (Thursday)

This session introduces **escalating interval training** — a format where the work-to-rest ratio progressively shifts in favour of work across the session, creating a cumulative metabolic demand that is significantly higher than standard interval training.

**Warm-up (8 minutes):** 5 minutes easy bike or treadmill, dynamic mobility sequence.

**Escalating Interval Protocol:**

*Round 1 — 1:2 Work-to-Rest Ratio (20 seconds work, 40 seconds rest)*
Complete 3 rounds of the following circuit:
- Rowing machine sprint
- Kettlebell swing (16–20 kg)
- Box jump or step-up
- Battle ropes

Rest 2 minutes after Round 1 is complete.

*Round 2 — 1:1 Work-to-Rest Ratio (30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest)*
Complete 3 rounds of the same circuit.
Rest 2 minutes.

*Round 3 — 2:1 Work-to-Rest Ratio (40 seconds work, 20 seconds rest)*
Complete 3 rounds of the same circuit.
Rest 2 minutes.

*Round 4 — Maximum Effort Block (45 seconds work, 15 seconds rest)*
Complete 2 rounds of the same circuit.

**Total conditioning work time:** approximately 28–32 minutes of intervals plus rest periods.

**Important monitoring note:** This is the most cardiovascularly demanding session in the entire 12-week programme. Heart rate will reach 85–90% of maximum during the 2:1 and maximum effort blocks. Monitor the client closely. If she shows signs of dizziness, nausea, or extreme pallor, reduce intensity immediately. Check blood glucose after this session without exception in Week 9.

**Cool-down:** 10 minutes. This session requires a longer cool-down than others. Walk on the treadmill for 5 minutes at a slow pace to bring heart rate down gradually, then 5 minutes of static stretching. An abrupt stop after this level of intensity can cause blood pressure to drop rapidly.

---

### Session 5 — Full Body Strength with AMRAP and Mechanical Drop Sets (Friday)

**Warm-up (10 minutes):** As per Session 1.

**Main Work:**

*Primary Movement 1 — Barbell Back Squat with AMRAP Final Set*
- Sets 1–3: 4 reps at 80% estimated max. Rest 2 minutes 30 seconds.
- Set 4 (AMRAP): Same weight, perform as many reps as possible with good form. Stop when form breaks down, not when it becomes uncomfortable. Record the rep count. This number becomes the benchmark to beat in Week 10.

*Primary Movement 2 — Incline Dumbbell Press with AMRAP Final Set*
- Sets 1–3: 8 reps at a challenging load. Rest 90 seconds.
- Set 4 (AMRAP): Same weight, maximum reps. Record.

*Mechanical Drop Set 1 — Bulgarian Split Squat into Reverse Lunge*
- Perform Bulgarian split squats to near-failure (approximately 10–12 reps), then immediately switch to reverse lunges with the same dumbbells and continue until near-failure again. That is one mechanical drop set. Complete 3 mechanical drop sets each leg. Rest 2 minutes between legs.

*Mechanical Drop Set 2 — Weighted Pull-Up into Lat Pulldown*
- If she can perform assisted weighted pull-ups, perform to near-failure, then immediately move to the lat pulldown machine and continue to near-failure. If pull-ups are not yet available, perform lat pulldown at a heavy load to near-failure, then reduce weight by 30% and continue. Complete 3 mechanical drop sets. Rest 90 seconds between sets.

*Superset — Shoulder Complex*
- **A1: Dumbbell Shoulder Press** — 3 sets × 10 reps. Rest 10 seconds.
- **A2: Lateral Raise** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Rest 10 seconds.
- **A3: Front Raise** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.

*Core Finisher:*
- **Weighted Plank** — 3 sets × 40 seconds. Place a weight plate on the lower back.
- **Cable Woodchop** — 3 sets × 12 reps each side. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Hanging Knee Raise or Leg Raise** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.

**Metabolic Finisher — Loaded Carry Complex (10 minutes):** As per previous sessions.

---

### Session 6 — Active Recovery (Saturday)

Active recovery in Phase 3 is more structured than in previous phases because the training volume and intensity are significantly higher. Recovery is not passive — it is an active process that must be managed as deliberately as the training sessions themselves.

**Morning:** 25–30 minute walk at genuinely easy pace. Heart rate should not exceed 100 bpm. This is not a workout — it is blood flow promotion and parasympathetic nervous system activation.

**Recovery session (30–40 minutes):**

- Foam rolling sequence — 90 seconds per area: quads, IT band, hamstrings, glutes, thoracic spine, lats, calves. Use a lacrosse ball for the glutes and upper back. Total: approximately 15 minutes.
- Stretching sequence — hold each position for 60 seconds: hip flexor stretch each side, pigeon pose each side, seated hamstring stretch each side, doorway chest stretch, lat stretch, thoracic rotation each side, child's pose.
- Optional: 10 minutes of guided breathing or meditation. As noted in the original programme, stress management is a legitimate component of glycaemic control. In Phase 3 with elevated training intensity, cortisol management becomes more important. Structured breathing (4 counts in, 4 counts hold, 6 counts out) activates the parasympathetic nervous system and has been shown to reduce cortisol and improve post-exercise recovery.

**Nutrition on active recovery day:** Slightly reduce carbohydrate intake compared to training days — approximately 20–30g less carbohydrate — as glycogen demands are lower. Maintain protein intake. This is a minor adjustment, not a significant dietary change.

---

## Week 10 — Load Progression

Week 10 applies the following progressions to the Week 9 framework:

**Strength sessions:**
- Increase all primary compound lift loads by 5%. This applies to the cluster set deadlift, hip thrust, barbell squat, and all contrast training loads.
- On AMRAP sets, attempt to beat the Week 9 rep count. If she achieved 6 reps on the squat AMRAP in Week 9, the goal is 7 reps in Week 10 with the same weight. If she achieves 8 or more reps, increase the weight by 2.5–5 kg for Week 11.
- Increase loaded carry distances by 5 metres on each carry variation.

**Conditioning sessions:**
- Density blocks: attempt to beat Week 9 round counts by at least half a round per block.
- Escalating intervals: add one additional round to Round 3 (the 2:1 work-to-rest block), making it 4 rounds instead of 3.

**Mechanical drop sets:**
- Increase the load on the primary exercise of each mechanical drop set by 5%. The secondary exercise load remains the same.

**Volume addition:**
- Add one additional working set to the primary compound movements in Sessions 1 and 3 (5 sets instead of 4 on contrast pairs and cluster sets).

---

Week 11 is the highest intensity week of the entire 12-week programme. Everything is pushed to its maximum within safe parameters.

### Key Changes in Week 11

**Loads:** Increase all primary compound lift loads by a further 5% from Week 10. These are the heaviest loads of the programme.

**AMRAP sets:** Perform AMRAP sets on the final set of every primary compound movement, not just selected exercises. This means AMRAP sets on the squat, deadlift, hip thrust, bench press, and lat pulldown in the same week.

**Conditioning sessions:** Both conditioning sessions use the Week 10 escalating interval format with the following addition — a **finisher round** after the maximum effort block consisting of 3 minutes of continuous work cycling through all four exercises with no rest. **Density blocks:** Reduce rest between blocks from 3 minutes to 2 minutes, increasing the overall metabolic demand of the session.

**Loaded carry finisher:** Increase to 12 minutes and add an overhead carry variation — walking with dumbbells held directly overhead, which demands exceptional core stability and shoulder endurance.

### Integrated Final Version — All Adjustments Incorporated

## Client Profile

**Age:** 45 | **Condition:** Type 2 Diabetes (Metformin) | **HbA1c:** 7.2% | **Goals:** Fat loss, glycaemic control improvement | **Setting:** Full gym access | **Additional protocols:** Fasted morning cardio, intermittent fasting (14:10 progressing to 16:8), weekly flex meal

---

> ## ⚠️ Master Clinical Advisory — Read Before Commencing
>
> Before this programme begins, the following must be confirmed without exception:
>
> **Medical clearance:** Obtain written GP clearance for moderate-to-vigorous exercise, high-intensity interval training, and intermittent fasting. This is not a standard disclaimer — it is a genuine clinical requirement for a type 2 diabetic client.
>
> **Medication confirmation:** Confirm full medication list. If she is on anything beyond Metformin — sulphonylureas, meglitinides, SGLT-2 inhibitors, or insulin — the fasted cardio, IF protocol, and high-intensity training in Phase 3 all carry additional risks that must be reviewed with her medical team before implementation.
>
> **Metformin timing:** GP must advise on Metformin timing adjustments to coincide with meals within the IF eating window. Metformin taken without food significantly increases gastrointestinal side effect risk.
>
> **HbA1c review:** Schedule a GP or diabetes nurse review at Week 6 and Week 12 to assess HbA1c response to the programme.
>
> **Hypoglycaemia protocol:** Despite Metformin's low hypoglycaemia risk, fast-acting glucose (glucose tablets, small carton of juice) must be accessible during every training session and every fasted morning cardio session throughout the programme.
>
> **Disordered eating screening:** Before implementing the IF protocol, informally assess whether the client has any history of disordered eating. If yes, the IF protocol is contraindicated regardless of metabolic benefit.
>
> **Blood glucose monitoring:** The client must own and use a blood glucose monitor throughout this programme. Monitoring protocols are specified for each phase.

---

## Programme Architecture

| Phase | Weeks | Primary Focus | Training Days | IF Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Foundation | 1–4 | Movement quality, metabolic baseline, habit formation | 4 main + 4–5 fasted cardio | 14:10 introduced Week 3 |
| 2 — Development | 5–8 | Progressive overload, upper/lower split, metabolic conditioning | 5 main + 4–5 fasted cardio | 14:10 progressing to 16:8 |
| 3 — Intensification | 9–12 | Maximum intensity, contrast training, cluster sets, peak week | 6 main + 5 fasted cardio | 16:8 modified |

---

## Universal Daily Protocols — Apply Throughout All 12 Weeks

### Blood Glucose Monitoring — Standard Protocol
- Upon waking
- Before fasted morning cardio
- After fasted morning cardio
- Before each main training session
- After each main training session
- Before bed

Intensive monitoring (all six checkpoints) applies throughout Phase 1, during the first two weeks of IF introduction, and during Week 11 peak week. Once patterns are established and stable, monitoring can be reduced to waking, pre-cardio, post-cardio, and before bed.

### Fasted Morning Cardio — Universal Rules
1. Check blood glucose before every session without exception
2. Below 5.0 mmol/L — do not perform fasted cardio. Consume 15g fast-acting carbohydrate, wait 15 minutes, retest. If above 5.0 mmol/L, gentle 15-minute walk only
3. 5.0–7.0 mmol/L — proceed as prescribed
4. 7.1–13.9 mmol/L — proceed at low-to-moderate intensity only. Likely Dawn Phenomenon. Log the reading
5. 14.0 mmol/L or above — do not exercise. Eat a balanced breakfast, take Metformin as prescribed, contact GP if readings are consistently this high
6. Drink 400–500 ml water before beginning
7. Black coffee only before the session — no milk, no sugar, no pre-workout supplements
8. Eat within 30–45 minutes of finishing every fasted cardio session
9. Check blood glucose after every session

### Fasted Morning Cardio — Intensity Parameters
- Modality: walking, stationary cycling, or elliptical only. No sprinting or high-intensity work in a fasted state
- Intensity: 45–60% maximum heart rate (79–105 bpm for this client)
- The client must be able to hold a full conversation throughout

### Flex Meal — Universal Rules
1. Always on a training day — never on a rest day
2. Always the evening meal — not lunch or breakfast
3. One meal, not one day — breakfast and lunch remain on-plan
4. Blood glucose check before and after (90 minutes post-meal)
5. Post-meal reading up to 10.0 mmol/L is acceptable. Above 12.0 mmol/L — note the meal and adjust future choices
6. Maximum two standard alcoholic drinks if applicable. Dry red wine preferred. Check blood glucose before bed if alcohol consumed — have a small low-GI snack if below 6.0 mmol/L
7. Return to normal nutrition plan at breakfast the following morning without guilt or compensation
8. Saturday evening is the recommended flex meal day throughout all phases

# PHASE 1 — FOUNDATION
## Weeks 1–4

---

## Phase 1 Goals
Establish movement patterns, build connective tissue tolerance, introduce consistent training stimulus, begin IF protocol at Week 3, and stabilise blood glucose responses to exercise and dietary changes. Fat loss in this phase is modest but metabolic adaptation begins immediately.

## Phase 1 Training Structure
**4 main sessions per week:** 2 full-body resistance sessions, 1 cardiovascular session, 1 active mobility session.
**Fasted morning cardio:** 4–5 mornings per week, 20–25 minutes, 45–55% max HR (79–96 bpm).
**Main session duration:** 45–55 minutes.

## Phase 1 IF Protocol
**Weeks 1–2:** No IF. Focus on establishing training and nutrition habits first.
**Week 3 onwards:** Introduce 14:10 time-restricted eating.
**Eating window:** 9:00 am – 7:00 pm
**Fasting window:** 7:00 pm – 9:00 am (14 hours)

During the fasting window: water, plain black coffee, and plain herbal tea only.

Metformin timing: take morning dose with the 9:00 am breakfast. Take evening dose with the last meal within the eating window. GP must confirm this adjustment.

Expected adaptation symptoms in the first one to two weeks of IF: hunger before 9:00 am, mild headaches, slight fatigue, mild irritability. All are normal and temporary. If dizziness, shakiness, sweating, or confusion occurs during the fasting window, check blood glucose immediately. If below 4.0 mmol/L, consume 15g fast-acting carbohydrate and contact GP.

## Phase 1 Weekly Schedule

| Day | Morning (Fasted Cardio) | Main Session |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Full Body Resistance A |
| Tuesday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Rest |
| Wednesday | 20–25 min fasted walk | MISS Cardio |
| Thursday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Full Body Resistance B |
| Friday | Rest | Rest |
| Saturday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Active Mobility + Flex Meal evening |
| Sunday | Complete rest | Complete rest |

Note on Wednesday: fasted cardio in the morning plus MISS cardio later in the day is acceptable in Phase 1 given the low intensity of both. If persistent fatigue develops, remove the Wednesday fasted session and keep only the main MISS session.

---

## Phase 1 Session Templates

### Full Body Resistance A

**Warm-up (8 minutes):**
5 minutes treadmill or bike at comfortable pace. Dynamic mobility: leg swings 10 each direction, hip circles 10 each direction, arm circles 10 each direction, bodyweight squats 10 reps, inchworm walk-outs 5 reps.

**Main Work:**

- **Goblet Squat** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Start with 6–8 kg dumbbell. Focus on depth, upright torso, controlled 3-second descent. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Cable Row** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Moderate weight. Full scapular retraction at end of each rep. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift** — 3 sets × 10 reps. 8–10 kg dumbbells. Hinge at hip, soft knee, feel hamstring stretch. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Chest Press (flat bench)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. 3-second lowering phase. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Plank Hold** — 3 sets × 20–30 seconds. Modify to knees if needed. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Banded Glute Bridge** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Light resistance band above knees. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down (5 minutes):**
Static stretching: hip flexors 45 seconds each side, hamstrings 45 seconds each side, chest 45 seconds, thoracic rotation 45 seconds each side.

---

### MISS Cardiovascular Session

**Format:** Moderate-Intensity Steady-State cardio.
**Duration:** 30 minutes (Week 1), 35 minutes (Weeks 2–3), 25 minutes (Week 4 deload).
**Modality:** Treadmill, stationary bike, or elliptical.
**Target heart rate:** 50–65% max HR (88–114 bpm).
**Intensity check:** The client should be able to hold a conversation throughout. If she cannot, reduce pace.

Check blood glucose before starting. If below 5.5 mmol/L, consume a small 15g carbohydrate snack and wait 15 minutes before beginning.

---

### Full Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Resistance A.

**Main Work:**

- **Leg Press (machine)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Feet shoulder-width, full range of motion. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Lat Pulldown (wide grip)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Pull to upper chest, controlled return. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Shoulder Press (seated)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Reverse Lunge** — 3 sets × 10 reps each leg. Bodyweight or very light dumbbells. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Cable Tricep Pushdown** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Full extension. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Bicep Curl** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Controlled tempo. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Dead Bug** — 3 sets × 8 reps each side. Lower back pressed to floor throughout. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Resistance A.

---

### Active Mobility Session

- 20-minute brisk walk (treadmill or outdoors, conversational pace)
- Cat-cow: 2 × 10 reps
- Child's pose: hold 60 seconds
- Pigeon pose each side: hold 45 seconds
- Supine spinal twist each side: hold 45 seconds
- Seated hamstring stretch each side: hold 45 seconds
- Foam rolling: quads, IT band, thoracic spine, calves — 60–90 seconds per area

Total time: approximately 40 minutes.

---

## Phase 1 Week-by-Week Progression

### Week 1
All sessions as per templates above. Loads are conservative — prioritise movement quality over weight. Log all loads used. MISS cardio 30 minutes.

### Week 2
Increase all resistance exercise loads by approximately 5% where form was solid in Week 1. Add 5 seconds to plank holds (25–35 seconds). MISS cardio increases to 35 minutes. No IF yet — continue establishing nutrition habits.

### Week 3
Introduce fourth set on primary compound movements: Goblet Squat, RDL, Leg Press, Lat Pulldown. Reduce rest periods on accessory exercises from 90 seconds to 75 seconds. MISS cardio remains 35 minutes — increase pace to keep heart rate at upper end of zone (105–114 bpm). **Introduce 14:10 IF protocol this week.** Intensive blood glucose monitoring at all six daily checkpoints for the first two weeks of IF.

### Week 4 — Deload
Reduce volume by 30%. Drop back to 3 sets on all exercises. Reduce loads by 10%. Shorten MISS cardio to 25 minutes. Reduce fasted morning cardio to 3 mornings, 15–20 minutes each. Continue 14:10 IF. Use this week to assess movement quality, note any areas of tightness or discomfort, and review blood glucose logs. Do not skip the deload — for a 45-year-old client with a metabolic condition, recovery is as important as the training stimulus.

---

# PHASE 2 — DEVELOPMENT
## Weeks 5–8

---

## Phase 2 Goals
Increase training frequency to five days per week, introduce upper/lower body splits, add metabolic conditioning, begin meaningful progressive overload, and progress IF from 14:10 to 16:8. Fat loss should become more visible and blood glucose responses to exercise should be more predictable.

## Phase 2 Training Structure
**5 main sessions per week:** 2 upper body resistance sessions, 2 lower body resistance sessions, 1 metabolic conditioning session.
**Fasted morning cardio:** 4–5 mornings per week, 25–30 minutes, 50–60% max HR (88–105 bpm).
**Main session duration:** 50–60 minutes.

## Phase 2 IF Protocol
**Weeks 5–6:** Continue 14:10 (9:00 am – 7:00 pm eating window).
**Weeks 7–8:** Progress to 16:8 if tolerating 14:10 well — stable blood glucose, no hypoglycaemic episodes, good energy, consistent training performance.
**16:8 eating window:** 10:00 am – 6:00 pm
**16:8 fasting window:** 6:00 pm – 10:00 am (16 hours)

**Modified 16:8 rule for training days:** On days with morning main training sessions, maintain 9:00 am eating window start (effectively 14:10) to ensure adequate fuelling. On days with afternoon or evening sessions, or rest days, apply 10:00 am start (16:8). This flexible approach prioritises performance and safety on heavy training days.

**Flex meal eating window extension:** On Saturday flex meal evenings, extend the eating window close by one hour (to 7:00 pm under 14:10, or 7:00 pm under 16:8) to allow a relaxed and social flex meal experience.

## Phase 2 Weekly Schedule

| Day | Morning (Fasted Cardio) | Main Session |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Upper Body Resistance A |
| Tuesday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Lower Body Resistance A |
| Wednesday | Rest morning | Metabolic Conditioning |
| Thursday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Upper Body Resistance B |
| Friday | Rest morning | Rest |
| Saturday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Lower Body Resistance B + Flex Meal evening |
| Sunday | Complete rest | Complete rest |

Note on Wednesday: fasted cardio is deliberately removed on metabolic conditioning mornings to ensure the client arrives at the conditioning session adequately fuelled and recovered.

---

5 minutes light cardio. Band pull-aparts 2 × 15, shoulder circles, thoracic rotations, 10 push-ups.

**Main Work:**

- **Barbell or Dumbbell Bench Press** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Moderate-to-heavy load. Rest 90 seconds.

- **Incline Dumbbell Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Overhead Tricep Extension (cable or dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** 5 minutes static stretching — chest, lats, shoulders, triceps.

---

5 minutes bike. Glute activation circuit: clamshells 2 × 15, banded lateral walks 2 × 10 each direction, bodyweight squats 2 × 10.

**Main Work:**

**Format:** Interval-based conditioning. Post-exercise glucose uptake is elevated for up to 24 hours following interval work.

3. Box step-ups (moderate height, alternating legs)
4. Kettlebell swing (12–16 kg)

**Target heart rate during work intervals:** 70–80% max HR (123–140 bpm).

**Cool-down (10 minutes):** Walk plus stretching.

Monitor heart rate throughout. If the client feels dizzy, lightheaded, or unusually fatigued, stop immediately and check blood glucose.

---

### Upper Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Upper Body A.

**Main Work:**

- **Incline Dumbbell Press** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Cable Row (close grip)** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Lateral Raise (dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Light weight, controlled. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Hammer Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Tricep Dips (assisted machine or bench)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Pallof Press (cable)** — 3 sets × 10 reps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Upper Body A.

---

### Lower Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Lower Body A.

**Main Work:**

- **Trap Bar Deadlift or Conventional Deadlift** — 4 sets × 6–8 reps. Primary strength movement of the week. Rest 2 minutes.
- **Bulgarian Split Squat (dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 10 reps each leg. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Hip Thrust (barbell or dumbbell)** — 4 sets × 12 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Leg Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Goblet Squat (tempo: 3-second descent)** — 3 sets × 10 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Plank with Shoulder Tap** — 3 sets × 10 taps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Lower Body A.

---

## Phase 2 Week-by-Week Progression

### Week 5
All sessions as per templates above. This is the first week of the upper/lower split — loads may feel conservative as the client adapts to the new structure. Log all loads.

### Week 6
Increase loads by 5% on all primary compound movements where three or more sets were completed with good form. Add one additional round to the metabolic conditioning interval block (22 minutes total work). Continue 14:10 IF.

### Week 7
Introduce supersets on accessory exercises to increase training density. Pair: bicep curls with tricep pushdowns, lateral raises with face pulls, leg curls with leg extensions. This reduces rest time between accessory work and elevates heart rate. Increase deadlift and squat loads by a further 5%. **Progress to 16:8 IF this week** if tolerating 14:10 well. Apply modified 16:8 rule based on training day timing.

### Week 8 — Deload
Reduce volume by 30%. Drop back to 3 sessions (one upper, one lower, one light cardio). Reduce loads by 10%. Reduce fasted morning cardio to 3 mornings, 15–20 minutes. Continue IF at whichever protocol the client is on. Use this week to reassess movement quality, review blood glucose logs, and prepare for Phase 3 intensity. Schedule mid-programme GP or diabetes nurse review this week if possible.

# Complete 12-Week Training & Nutrition Programme
### Integrated Final Version — All Adjustments Incorporated

---

## Client Profile

**Age:** 45 | **Condition:** Type 2 Diabetes (Metformin) | **HbA1c:** 7.2% | **Goals:** Fat loss, glycaemic control improvement | **Setting:** Full gym access | **Additional protocols:** Fasted morning cardio, intermittent fasting (14:10 progressing to 16:8), weekly flex meal

---

> ## ⚠️ Master Clinical Advisory — Read Before Commencing
>
> Before this programme begins, the following must be confirmed without exception:
>
> **Medical clearance:** Obtain written GP clearance for moderate-to-vigorous exercise, high-intensity interval training, and intermittent fasting. This is not a standard disclaimer — it is a genuine clinical requirement for a type 2 diabetic client.
>
> **Medication confirmation:** Confirm full medication list. If she is on anything beyond Metformin — sulphonylureas, meglitinides, SGLT-2 inhibitors, or insulin — the fasted cardio, IF protocol, and high-intensity training in Phase 3 all carry additional risks that must be reviewed with her medical team before implementation.
>
> **Metformin timing:** GP must advise on Metformin timing adjustments to coincide with meals within the IF eating window. Metformin taken without food significantly increases gastrointestinal side effect risk.
>
> **HbA1c review:** Schedule a GP or diabetes nurse review at Week 6 and Week 12 to assess HbA1c response to the programme.
>
> **Hypoglycaemia protocol:** Despite Metformin's low hypoglycaemia risk, fast-acting glucose (glucose tablets, small carton of juice) must be accessible during every training session and every fasted morning cardio session throughout the programme.
>
> **Disordered eating screening:** Before implementing the IF protocol, informally assess whether the client has any history of disordered eating. If yes, the IF protocol is contraindicated regardless of metabolic benefit.
>
> **Blood glucose monitoring:** The client must own and use a blood glucose monitor throughout this programme. Monitoring protocols are specified for each phase.

---

## Programme Architecture

| Phase | Weeks | Primary Focus | Training Days | IF Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Foundation | 1–4 | Movement quality, metabolic baseline, habit formation | 4 main + 4–5 fasted cardio | 14:10 introduced Week 3 |
| 2 — Development | 5–8 | Progressive overload, upper/lower split, metabolic conditioning | 5 main + 4–5 fasted cardio | 14:10 progressing to 16:8 |
| 3 — Intensification | 9–12 | Maximum intensity, contrast training, cluster sets, peak week | 6 main + 5 fasted cardio | 16:8 modified |

---

## Universal Daily Protocols — Apply Throughout All 12 Weeks

### Blood Glucose Monitoring — Standard Protocol
- Upon waking
- Before fasted morning cardio
- After fasted morning cardio
- Before each main training session
- After each main training session
- Before bed

Intensive monitoring (all six checkpoints) applies throughout Phase 1, during the first two weeks of IF introduction, and during Week 11 peak week. Once patterns are established and stable, monitoring can be reduced to waking, pre-cardio, post-cardio, and before bed.

### Fasted Morning Cardio — Universal Rules
1. Check blood glucose before every session without exception
2. Below 5.0 mmol/L — do not perform fasted cardio. Consume 15g fast-acting carbohydrate, wait 15 minutes, retest. If above 5.0 mmol/L, gentle 15-minute walk only
3. 5.0–7.0 mmol/L — proceed as prescribed
4. 7.1–13.9 mmol/L — proceed at low-to-moderate intensity only. Likely Dawn Phenomenon. Log the reading
5. 14.0 mmol/L or above — do not exercise. Eat a balanced breakfast, take Metformin as prescribed, contact GP if readings are consistently this high
6. Drink 400–500 ml water before beginning
7. Black coffee only before the session — no milk, no sugar, no pre-workout supplements
8. Eat within 30–45 minutes of finishing every fasted cardio session
9. Check blood glucose after every session

### Fasted Morning Cardio — Intensity Parameters
- Modality: walking, stationary cycling, or elliptical only. No sprinting or high-intensity work in a fasted state
- Intensity: 45–60% maximum heart rate (79–105 bpm for this client)
- The client must be able to hold a full conversation throughout

### Flex Meal — Universal Rules
1. Always on a training day — never on a rest day
2. Always the evening meal — not lunch or breakfast
3. One meal, not one day — breakfast and lunch remain on-plan
4. Blood glucose check before and after (90 minutes post-meal)
5. Post-meal reading up to 10.0 mmol/L is acceptable. Above 12.0 mmol/L — note the meal and adjust future choices
6. Maximum two standard alcoholic drinks if applicable. Dry red wine preferred. Check blood glucose before bed if alcohol consumed — have a small low-GI snack if below 6.0 mmol/L
7. Return to normal nutrition plan at breakfast the following morning without guilt or compensation
8. Saturday evening is the recommended flex meal day throughout all phases

---

---

# PHASE 1 — FOUNDATION
## Weeks 1–4

---

## Phase 1 Goals
Establish movement patterns, build connective tissue tolerance, introduce consistent training stimulus, begin IF protocol at Week 3, and stabilise blood glucose responses to exercise and dietary changes. Fat loss in this phase is modest but metabolic adaptation begins immediately.

## Phase 1 Training Structure
**4 main sessions per week:** 2 full-body resistance sessions, 1 cardiovascular session, 1 active mobility session.
**Fasted morning cardio:** 4–5 mornings per week, 20–25 minutes, 45–55% max HR (79–96 bpm).
**Main session duration:** 45–55 minutes.

## Phase 1 IF Protocol
**Weeks 1–2:** No IF. Focus on establishing training and nutrition habits first.
**Week 3 onwards:** Introduce 14:10 time-restricted eating.
**Eating window:** 9:00 am – 7:00 pm
**Fasting window:** 7:00 pm – 9:00 am (14 hours)

During the fasting window: water, plain black coffee, and plain herbal tea only.

Metformin timing: take morning dose with the 9:00 am breakfast. Take evening dose with the last meal within the eating window. GP must confirm this adjustment.

Expected adaptation symptoms in the first one to two weeks of IF: hunger before 9:00 am, mild headaches, slight fatigue, mild irritability. All are normal and temporary. If dizziness, shakiness, sweating, or confusion occurs during the fasting window, check blood glucose immediately. If below 4.0 mmol/L, consume 15g fast-acting carbohydrate and contact GP.

## Phase 1 Weekly Schedule

| Day | Morning (Fasted Cardio) | Main Session |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Full Body Resistance A |
| Tuesday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Rest |
| Wednesday | 20–25 min fasted walk | MISS Cardio |
| Thursday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Full Body Resistance B |
| Friday | Rest | Rest |
| Saturday | 20–25 min fasted walk | Active Mobility + Flex Meal evening |
| Sunday | Complete rest | Complete rest |

Note on Wednesday: fasted cardio in the morning plus MISS cardio later in the day is acceptable in Phase 1 given the low intensity of both. If persistent fatigue develops, remove the Wednesday fasted session and keep only the main MISS session.

---

## Phase 1 Session Templates

### Full Body Resistance A

**Warm-up (8 minutes):**
5 minutes treadmill or bike at comfortable pace. Dynamic mobility: leg swings 10 each direction, hip circles 10 each direction, arm circles 10 each direction, bodyweight squats 10 reps, inchworm walk-outs 5 reps.

**Main Work:**

- **Goblet Squat** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Start with 6–8 kg dumbbell. Focus on depth, upright torso, controlled 3-second descent. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Cable Row** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Moderate weight. Full scapular retraction at end of each rep. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift** — 3 sets × 10 reps. 8–10 kg dumbbells. Hinge at hip, soft knee, feel hamstring stretch. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Chest Press (flat bench)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. 3-second lowering phase. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Plank Hold** — 3 sets × 20–30 seconds. Modify to knees if needed. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Banded Glute Bridge** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Light resistance band above knees. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down (5 minutes):**
Static stretching: hip flexors 45 seconds each side, hamstrings 45 seconds each side, chest 45 seconds, thoracic rotation 45 seconds each side.

---

### MISS Cardiovascular Session

**Format:** Moderate-Intensity Steady-State cardio.
**Duration:** 30 minutes (Week 1), 35 minutes (Weeks 2–3), 25 minutes (Week 4 deload).
**Modality:** Treadmill, stationary bike, or elliptical.
**Target heart rate:** 50–65% max HR (88–114 bpm).
**Intensity check:** The client should be able to hold a conversation throughout. If she cannot, reduce pace.

Check blood glucose before starting. If below 5.5 mmol/L, consume a small 15g carbohydrate snack and wait 15 minutes before beginning.

---

### Full Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Resistance A.

**Main Work:**

- **Leg Press (machine)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Feet shoulder-width, full range of motion. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Lat Pulldown (wide grip)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Pull to upper chest, controlled return. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Shoulder Press (seated)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Reverse Lunge** — 3 sets × 10 reps each leg. Bodyweight or very light dumbbells. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Cable Tricep Pushdown** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Full extension. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Dumbbell Bicep Curl** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Controlled tempo. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Dead Bug** — 3 sets × 8 reps each side. Lower back pressed to floor throughout. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Resistance A.

---

### Active Mobility Session

- 20-minute brisk walk (treadmill or outdoors, conversational pace)
- Cat-cow: 2 × 10 reps
- Child's pose: hold 60 seconds
- Pigeon pose each side: hold 45 seconds
- Supine spinal twist each side: hold 45 seconds
- Seated hamstring stretch each side: hold 45 seconds
- Foam rolling: quads, IT band, thoracic spine, calves — 60–90 seconds per area

Total time: approximately 40 minutes.

---

## Phase 1 Week-by-Week Progression

### Week 1
All sessions as per templates above. Loads are conservative — prioritise movement quality over weight. Log all loads used. MISS cardio 30 minutes.

### Week 2
Increase all resistance exercise loads by approximately 5% where form was solid in Week 1. Add 5 seconds to plank holds (25–35 seconds). MISS cardio increases to 35 minutes. No IF yet — continue establishing nutrition habits.

### Week 3
Introduce fourth set on primary compound movements: Goblet Squat, RDL, Leg Press, Lat Pulldown. Reduce rest periods on accessory exercises from 90 seconds to 75 seconds. MISS cardio remains 35 minutes — increase pace to keep heart rate at upper end of zone (105–114 bpm). **Introduce 14:10 IF protocol this week.** Intensive blood glucose monitoring at all six daily checkpoints for the first two weeks of IF.

### Week 4 — Deload
Reduce volume by 30%. Drop back to 3 sets on all exercises. Reduce loads by 10%. Shorten MISS cardio to 25 minutes. Reduce fasted morning cardio to 3 mornings, 15–20 minutes each. Continue 14:10 IF. Use this week to assess movement quality, note any areas of tightness or discomfort, and review blood glucose logs. Do not skip the deload — for a 45-year-old client with a metabolic condition, recovery is as important as the training stimulus.

---

---

# PHASE 2 — DEVELOPMENT
## Weeks 5–8

---

## Phase 2 Goals
Increase training frequency to five days per week, introduce upper/lower body splits, add metabolic conditioning, begin meaningful progressive overload, and progress IF from 14:10 to 16:8. Fat loss should become more visible and blood glucose responses to exercise should be more predictable.

## Phase 2 Training Structure
**5 main sessions per week:** 2 upper body resistance sessions, 2 lower body resistance sessions, 1 metabolic conditioning session.
**Fasted morning cardio:** 4–5 mornings per week, 25–30 minutes, 50–60% max HR (88–105 bpm).
**Main session duration:** 50–60 minutes.

## Phase 2 IF Protocol
**Weeks 5–6:** Continue 14:10 (9:00 am – 7:00 pm eating window).
**Weeks 7–8:** Progress to 16:8 if tolerating 14:10 well — stable blood glucose, no hypoglycaemic episodes, good energy, consistent training performance.
**16:8 eating window:** 10:00 am – 6:00 pm
**16:8 fasting window:** 6:00 pm – 10:00 am (16 hours)

**Modified 16:8 rule for training days:** On days with morning main training sessions, maintain 9:00 am eating window start (effectively 14:10) to ensure adequate fuelling. On days with afternoon or evening sessions, or rest days, apply 10:00 am start (16:8). This flexible approach prioritises performance and safety on heavy training days.

**Flex meal eating window extension:** On Saturday flex meal evenings, extend the eating window close by one hour (to 7:00 pm under 14:10, or 7:00 pm under 16:8) to allow a relaxed and social flex meal experience.

## Phase 2 Weekly Schedule

| Day | Morning (Fasted Cardio) | Main Session |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Upper Body Resistance A |
| Tuesday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Lower Body Resistance A |
| Wednesday | Rest morning | Metabolic Conditioning |
| Thursday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Upper Body Resistance B |
| Friday | Rest morning | Rest |
| Saturday | 25–30 min fasted walk/cycle | Lower Body Resistance B + Flex Meal evening |
| Sunday | Complete rest | Complete rest |

Note on Wednesday: fasted cardio is deliberately removed on metabolic conditioning mornings to ensure the client arrives at the conditioning session adequately fuelled and recovered.

---

## Phase 2 Session Templates

### Upper Body Resistance A

**Warm-up (8 minutes):**
5 minutes light cardio. Band pull-aparts 2 × 15, shoulder circles, thoracic rotations, 10 push-ups.

**Main Work:**

- **Barbell or Dumbbell Bench Press** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Moderate-to-heavy load. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Bent-Over Dumbbell Row** — 4 sets × 10 reps each arm. Controlled, full range. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Cable Face Pull** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Light weight, external rotation emphasis. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Incline Dumbbell Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Overhead Tricep Extension (cable or dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** 5 minutes static stretching — chest, lats, shoulders, triceps.

---

### Lower Body Resistance A

**Warm-up (8 minutes):**
5 minutes bike. Glute activation circuit: clamshells 2 × 15, banded lateral walks 2 × 10 each direction, bodyweight squats 2 × 10.

**Main Work:**

- **Barbell Back Squat or Goblet Squat (progressed load)** — 4 sets × 8 reps. Rest 2 minutes. Continue with goblet squat if back squat technique is not yet solid.
- **Romanian Deadlift (barbell or dumbbells)** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Walking Lunges** — 3 sets × 12 reps each leg. Bodyweight or light dumbbells. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Leg Curl (machine)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Leg Extension (machine)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Standing Calf Raise** — 3 sets × 20 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Cable Woodchop** — 3 sets × 10 reps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** 5 minutes static stretching — hip flexors, hamstrings, quads, glutes.

---

### Metabolic Conditioning Session

**Format:** Interval-based conditioning. Post-exercise glucose uptake is elevated for up to 24 hours following interval work.

**Warm-up (5 minutes):** Light bike or treadmill walk.

**Interval Block (20 minutes):**
40 seconds work / 20 seconds rest, cycling continuously through:
1. Rowing machine (moderate-high effort)
2. Battle ropes or fast-paced stationary bike
3. Box step-ups (moderate height, alternating legs)
4. Kettlebell swing (12–16 kg)

**Target heart rate during work intervals:** 70–80% max HR (123–140 bpm).

**Cool-down (10 minutes):** Walk plus stretching.

Monitor heart rate throughout. If the client feels dizzy, lightheaded, or unusually fatigued, stop immediately and check blood glucose.

---

### Upper Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Upper Body A.

**Main Work:**

- **Incline Dumbbell Press** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Cable Row (close grip)** — 4 sets × 10 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Lateral Raise (dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 15 reps. Light weight, controlled. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Hammer Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Tricep Dips (assisted machine or bench)** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 60 seconds.
- **Pallof Press (cable)** — 3 sets × 10 reps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Upper Body A.

---

### Lower Body Resistance B

**Warm-up:** As per Lower Body A.

**Main Work:**

- **Trap Bar Deadlift or Conventional Deadlift** — 4 sets × 6–8 reps. Primary strength movement of the week. Rest 2 minutes.
- **Bulgarian Split Squat (dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 10 reps each leg. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Hip Thrust (barbell or dumbbell)** — 4 sets × 12 reps. Rest 90 seconds.
- **Seated Leg Curl** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Goblet Squat (tempo: 3-second descent)** — 3 sets × 10 reps. Rest 75 seconds.
- **Plank with Shoulder Tap** — 3 sets × 10 taps each side. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down:** As per Lower Body A.

---

## Phase 2 Week-by-Week Progression

### Week 5
All sessions as per templates above. This is the first week of the upper/lower split — loads may feel conservative as the client adapts to the new structure. Log all loads.

### Week 6
Increase loads by 5% on all primary compound movements where three or more sets were completed with good form. Add one additional round to the metabolic conditioning interval block (22 minutes total work). Continue 14:10 IF.

### Week 7
Introduce supersets on accessory exercises to increase training density. Pair: bicep curls with tricep pushdowns, lateral raises with face pulls, leg curls with leg extensions. This reduces rest time between accessory work and elevates heart rate. Increase deadlift and squat loads by a further 5%. **Progress to 16:8 IF this week** if tolerating 14:10 well. Apply modified 16:8 rule based on training day timing.

### Week 8 — Deload
Reduce volume by 30%. Drop back to 3 sessions (one upper, one lower, one light cardio). Reduce loads by 10%. Reduce fasted morning cardio to 3 mornings, 15–20 minutes. Continue IF at whichever protocol the client is on. Use this week to reassess movement quality, review blood glucose logs, and prepare for Phase 3 intensity. Schedule mid-programme GP or diabetes nurse review this week if possible.
